These methods highlight the interplay between search behavior, navigation patterns, and user interaction in both structured and unstructured environments, offering insights into how users explore and retrieve information in complex networks.

These systems use interaction logs to build richer user models and identify behavioral patterns, which are then used to form visitor clusters. Sequence-aware recommender systems utilize interaction logs to provide contextually relevant recommendations. Additionally, sequence-to-sequence models are employed to enhance session-based query suggestions by leveraging session context, query-aware attention, and copy mechanisms. These methods improve the accuracy and personalization of recommendations by integrating sequential data, user modeling, and behavioral clustering.

Markov models are widely used to capture movement patterns, while data-driven methods leverage real-world datasets and validation techniques to enhance accuracy. Multi-modal learning integrates diverse data sources, such as on-device behavioral data, to improve prediction tasks like next venue or trip destination forecasting. Trends emphasize the use of mobility meta-attributes, fine-grained data, and task-specific granularity to refine model effectiveness. These approaches are applied in urban planning, transportation, and public health, highlighting the integration of mobility data with computational and epidemiological models.
